public_rationale: Independent author accounts document a wave of discovery reports beginning March 20, including repeated Bluesky posts, reports from multiple writer friends, and an original scholarly discussion post. This supports the ordinary qualitative claim that many authors were reporting similar discoveries. It does not verify every author's conclusion that Meta used each listed work.
limitations: The evidence establishes widespread reports qualitatively, not a measured share of social media.
Katsu's account includes March 21 as well as March 20.
Original reports establish what authors reported, not whether their underlying training-use inferences were correct.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many other authors are discovering that Meta used their works from the pirated database.

statement.excerpt: Many other authors are discovering the same thing; social media is full of reports like mine.
statement.document_title: Meta pirated at least 101 of my books and articles, and tens of millions of others

from_speaker: social media is full of reports like mine
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that numerous other authors were publicly reporting discoveries of their works in LibGen and associating those discoveries with Meta's reported use.
This assesses the existence and breadth of those reports, not whether each author's inference about actual training use was correct.
Many and full are ordinary qualitative descriptions of widespread discussion, not a numerical threshold or a claim about all social-media users.

For the ongoing observation, use March 2025 through the post date as the current reporting period. Later publications may document events within that period, but later discoveries alone cannot support it.
criteria.support_condition: Dated author accounts and contemporaneous reporting establish numerous independent discovery reports circulating by March 20, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive contemporaneous record establishes that reports were isolated or that the claimed wave began only after March 20.

evidence.excerpt: On Thursday and Friday morning, author after author was searching the site, then posting on Bluesky: OMG.
evidence.explanation: Katsu explicitly places the start of repeated author discovery posts on Thursday, March 20. Her account also covers Friday; only its Thursday component bears on the target period.

evidence.excerpt: One of my writer friends said a couple of her books were there. Another had 15 of her 19 books pirated on LibGen.
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning One of my writer friends
evidence.explanation: This same-day account describes separate discoveries by writer friends. The surrounding post also describes Roysdon's own search and a broader wave of public reports.

evidence.excerpt: I found two articles of mine from Monumenta Nipponica and two from Japanese Journal of Religious Studies.
evidence.publisher: Ross Bender, PMJS public discussion group
evidence.explanation: This original public message independently demonstrates a scholar reporting discovery of his own works after reading the Atlantic investigation. It corroborates the occurrence of reports, not Meta's use of those particular files.
